subject: Proposal: Shift to annual prepay with performance-tied rebates
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@brightbridge.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.co@redwood.inference>
Cc: BrightBridge AI Procurement <procurement@brightbridge.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Moving to annual prepay — looking for structure for 2yr term with performance protections

Hi Marissa,

We're looking at consolidating our monthly usage into an annual prepay for 2027–2028 and want to understand what a multi-year arrangement with Redwood would look like. A few things on our side:

- We expect 30% QoQ growth next year as we ramp model usage across product.
- Procurement needs predictable invoicing and a PO-ready contract (net 30 preferred).
- Legal will push back on steep early-termination exposure; we need a stepdown/true-up approach that protects our startup cash profile if we miss the ramp.

Can you share a suggested structure: tiered discount by committed ARR, ramp milestones tied to partial rebate or credit, and billing cadence (one invoice vs yearly installments)? Also, we may need evidence of data residency controls for renewals — happy to loop in security later.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Zhao
VP Product, BrightBridge AI
emily.zhao@brightbridge.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.co@redwood.inference>

Subject: Re: Moving to annual prepay — looking for structure for 2yr term with performance protections

Hi Emily — great to hear from you and congrats on the product ramp. I sketched two practical approaches that customers commonly use; attaching a brief term sheet and a simple model that shows net economics across scenarios. High level:

Option A — Annual Prepay, 2-year term
- 12-month prepay invoice upfront for year 1, 12-month prepay invoice for year 2 (option to invoice both up front if preferred)
- Discount tiers: 12% at $1.2M ARR; 16% at $2.5M ARR; 20% at $5M+ ARR
- Ramp protection: if actual consumption in a year is below 70% of committed, customer receives a pro-rata credit equal to 50% of the unused prepay (applied as account credit) rather than full refund; credit expires after 12 months

Option B — Annual Prepay with performance-tied rebates
- Similar discounts but 6–8% of ARR reserved as a contingent rebate pool tied to agreed milestones (usage or product launches) paid at end of year 1 if milestones met; otherwise rebate converts to account credits spread across year 2

Other notes:
- We can do a stepdown true-up schedule (24% stepdown over 12 months) to reduce early-termination exposure for you — this is commonly accepted in enterprise deals.
- Net-30 invoice terms are fine. We prefer payment in full for each prepaid year to retain discount levels; if you need staged payments we can propose a small premium to compensate.

I'm attaching: RBW-term-sheet-BB-v3.pdf (term sheet) and BrightBridge-pricing-model.xlsx (simple scenarios). If this looks good, I can loop in Ben and Finance for final concession approval and send a draft SOW/PO-ready agreement.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa — thanks for the context. Quick thoughts:

- Discount bands: the 12/16/20% progression is reasonable. For BrightBridge I would start at the 16% band as an anchor and offer 18% if they commit to both years up front or provide a shorter onboarding SLA (we can swap onboarding credits for discount).
- Rebate pool (Option B) is attractive because it keeps cash in our hands and only pays out on delivery. Recommend capping the contingent pool at 7% of year-1 ARR and tying to 2–3 objective milestones (e.g., product integration completed, bulk inference traffic hitting X rps, success metric for latency/cost per call).
- Stepdown true-up: suggest a 9-month linear stepdown with a 25% protection floor for year-1 (i.e., maximum credit exposure = 25% of prepay) so we avoid big churn hits.
- Legal: ask for a clause allowing us to net unused credits against overage in year 2 if they significantly exceed committed usage.

I'll approve the approach pending Priyom's numbers and a short note from RevOps confirming invoicing mechanics (PO -> invoice -> applied credit).

Ben

Attaching a quick model (BrightBridge-pricing-model.xlsx) with three scenarios: conservative ramp (50% year-1), expected (80% year-1), and aggressive (120% year-1). Notes:

- With a 7% contingent rebate pool, our downside at 50% ramp is a 4.2% effective hit to ARR in year 1 (manageable).
- Account-credit-only refunds materially lower cash risk; operationally we can apply credits automatically and they expire after 12 months — this meets internal revenue recognition constraints if we structure it as contra-revenue/credit memo.
- If they want staged payments instead of full prepay for year 2, we should price a 2% premium on the discount to preserve unit economics.

Marissa — thanks to you, Ben and Priyom for the quick turnaround. We discussed internally and are prepared to move forward with Option B (annual prepay with a performance-tied rebate pool) with a few clarifications: 

- We will prepay year 1 in full on signature. For year 2 we prefer an invoice at start of year 2 (not prepay) but will accept a 2% premium if Redwood requires advance payment to maintain the 18% discount.
- Contingent rebate pool capped at 6% of year-1 ARR, paid at the year-end milestone review. If milestones are not met, the rebate converts to account credits usable in year 2 only.
- Stepdown true-up acceptable with a 9-month linear stepdown and a 25% protection floor as proposed.
- Procurement will issue a PO upon receipt of a PO-ready agreement and DocuSign link.

Please send a PO-ready agreement and the DocuSign link and we'll get procurement moving. Appreciate the flexibility on credits vs refunds — that helps our cash plans.

Emily Zhao
VP Product, BrightBridge AI
